conflicts.issue: Realistic vs. Aspirational 2030 Clean Energy Targets in EAB Renewable Energy Resolution
conflicts.summary: Committee members expressed differing views on the Environmental Affairs Board's proposed Renewable Energy Resolution regarding whether an 80% renewable energy target by 2030 was realistic or overly aspirational.
conflicts.side_a_position: Prefer realistic, achievable deadlines and clear operational scope before making formal commitments.
side_a_arguments: Questioned whether transitioning to 80% renewable energy in under 12 years (by 2030) is realistic rather than purely aspirational.
Sought clarification on whether the resolution bound the entire community or only City and County operations, noting formal calls on external actors should remain realistic.
conflicts.side_b_position: Support moving forward with an aspirational clean energy resolution and joint City-County planning.
side_b_arguments: Viewed the resolution as an aspirational policy commitment similar to California's 100% clean energy executive order aimed at spurring technology.
Supported advancing joint City and County planning work with staff and managers rather than delaying.
conflicts.resolution: EAB presenter Casey Collins clarified the binding portion only committed to developing a plan for City and County operations; discussion continued into manager updates before the transcript digest truncated with no formal vote recorded.

meetings.title: Joint City-County Committee
meetings.executive_summary: At the September 11, 2018 Joint City-County Committee meeting (presided over by an unnamed chair standing in for Mayor Steve Schewel), members approved the May 8, 2018 meeting minutes by unanimous voice vote. The committee then heard an Environmental Affairs Board presentation and public comment on a proposed Renewable Energy Resolution targeting 80% clean energy for City and County operations by 2030 and 100% by 2050, sparking discussion over realistic versus aspirational timelines before a truncated gap in the transcript digest. Following updates on a nonviolent expunction and driver's license restoration pilot, Commissioner Wendy Jacobs and staff reviewed FY19 eviction diversion investments—$90,000 in new County funding plus Opening Doors assistance alongside $200,000 in City funding for Legal Aid of North Carolina—and members reached consensus without a formal vote to have City and County attorneys review the joint Code of Ethics. The meeting concluded with a comprehensive Hurricane Florence emergency preparedness briefing covering six government-staffed shelters, Service Level 3 dispatch limits, road-clearing coordination, and multilingual public safety messaging prior to adjournment at 11:13 AM.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Approval of May 8, 2018 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The presiding chair opened the meeting at 9:05 AM, noting they were presiding in place of Mayor Steve Schewel and reminding attendees to prepare supplies and fuel for the approaching hurricane. After waiting briefly for Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton to return to the room, the committee considered the May 8, 2018 minutes. A motion and second were made and approved by voice vote with no opposition.

agenda_items.title: Environmental Affairs Board Renewable Energy Resolution Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Casey Collins of the Environmental Affairs Board (EAB) presented a resolution committing Durham to develop a plan for City and County operations to transition to renewable energy—targeting 80% by 2030 and 100% by 2050—while urging state, federal, and utility action. One public speaker supported prompt passage despite incomplete implementation plans, citing climate urgency and technical feasibility. Committee members debated whether the 2030 target was realistic rather than aspirational, clarified that the binding commitment applied to planning for City and County operations rather than the whole community, and asked City and County managers for a status update on a joint plan (referencing $30,000 each) before the digest truncated.

agenda_items.title: Expunction and Driver's License Restoration Pilot Program
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after a truncated middle section of the transcript, presenters discussed evaluating pilot programs and bringing back recommendations to the committee. In response to member questions regarding the model participant for the expunction and driver's license restoration initiative, presenters explained the program targets nonviolent, first- or second-time offenders. Eligibility developed with the District Attorney covers individuals whose licenses were suspended for more than 18 months, excluding DWI and certain offenses such as hit-and-run.

agenda_items.title: Eviction Diversion Funding Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Initiated by Commissioner Wendy Jacobs to align City and County efforts following FY19 budget adoption, County staff reported approving $90,000 above base funding for eviction diversion alongside Opening Doors and coordinated entry rental assistance, serving 589 individuals and families in the first two months. City Community Development Director Reginald Johnson reported that City Council appropriated $200,000 in FY19 to support a Legal Aid of North Carolina eviction diversion pilot funding two attorneys, a paralegal, and an outreach coordinator. Staff noted they were finalizing the Legal Aid contract scope of work.

agenda_items.title: Evaluate City-County Code of Ethics for Boards, Committees, and Commissions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Committee members discussed having the City Attorney and County Attorney compare existing ethics codes and prepare proposed revisions, particularly governing joint City-County boards and commissions. A member offered a motion directing the respective attorneys to review the code and draft revisions, and asked whether a formal vote was required or if staff could simply proceed. Members agreed by consensus to direct the attorneys without a formal vote and requested the item return on the next meeting's agenda.

agenda_items.title: Hurricane Florence Emergency Preparedness Briefing and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Emergency management staff briefed the committee on Hurricane Florence preparations, outlining evacuation shelters (including Walltown, a northern site, and Campus Hills Recreation Center at 7 sq. ft. per person) and long-term shelters at Northern, Hillside, Riverside, and Southern high schools staffed by DSS and public health employees because Red Cross staff were deployed elsewhere. Officials explained that high winds could trigger Service Level 3 operations suspending fire, EMS, and law enforcement dispatches unless overridden by a department chief, while DOT, local crews, and the Forest Service coordinated road-clearing duties. Members urged clear public messaging on downed power lines, floodwaters, and generator safety, with staff confirming Spanish translation at the EOC and three-deep 12-hour staff shifts before the meeting adjourned at 11:13 AM.

votes.notes: Individual mover, seconder, and full attendance roll call were not named in the transcript digest.
votes.discussion_detail: After briefly waiting for Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton to return to the chamber, a motion and second were made to approve the May 8, 2018 Joint City-County Committee minutes (referred to in ASR text at 00:01:10 as May 18, 2018). No opposition was raised on the voice vote.
